Hence, the correct answer is **option 2**.

**Corrected sentence:** *Santa Claus stays at the North Pole when he isn’t out delivering__ gifts for Christmas.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

The **__reported alarm__** of the earthquake scared every citizen of the country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"alarming report."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **"Alarming"** is an adjective that means causing alarm or fear. (चिंताजनक, भयप्रद)
 
• In the sentence, we need an adjective to describe the type of report, not a noun to describe the citizens' reaction.
 
• **"Alarming report"** correctly conveys that the report itself caused fear.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

**Correct sentence**: *The **alarming report**__ of the earthquake scared every citizen of the country.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2, "alarmed report,"** does not make grammatical sense because "alarmed" is an adjective that describes a person who is feeling fear or distress, not a report.
 
• **Option 3, "reporting alarm," **changes the sentence structure and meaning by suggesting that the earthquake is currently happening and being reported on, rather than that a report about the earthquake caused fear.
 
• **Option 4, "alarm reporting,"** is a gerund phrase that also changes the sentence structure and does not make sense in context.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'carried away'**.

• Let us look into the **meanings **of the **given options **- 
 
 
• **carried off - **to succeed in doing or achieving something difficult
 
• **carried away - **to arouse to a high and often excessive degree of emotion or enthusiasm.
 
• **carried of - **to take or bear (something) from one place to another. (*Note - this is not a phrasal verb)*
 
• **carried to - **support and move (someone or something) from one place to another. (*Note - this is not a phrasal verb)*

**Correct sentence__ - ***I was **__carried away__** by her rapturous song.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

The Delhi Birla International School __alumnus occupy__ leading positions in different areas of profession and service.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'alumni occupy'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the** present indefinite tense.** Therefore, option 2 gets eliminated.
 
• **'Alumnus'** means "a former male student of a school, college or university".
 
 
• **E.g.** Imran has received numerous job offers because he’s an alumnus of an elite medical school.
 
 
 
• **'Alumni'** means "​the former male and female students of a school, college or university".
 
 
• **E.g.** Several of the class of 1992 alumni donated money to their classmate’s account when he became ill last winter.
 
 
 
• The given sentence is **not **talking about a single student as is clear from **'leading positions in different areas'.**
 
• Therefore, we cannot use '**alumnus**'. 
 
• According to the rule and examples that are given above,** 'alumni occupy'** will be used in the **underlined part** of the given sentence.

 ​

**Correct Sentence__:** *The Delhi Birla International School **alumni occupy** leading positions in different areas of profession and service.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Indefinite Tense** represents an action which is regular or normal or true and uses the base form of the verb.
 
• In the present indefinite tense **'s/es'** is used with the base form of the verb if the subject is **"third-person singular".**
 
 
• **E.g.** My father **goes** for a walk daily.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully:**

Shakespeare was both a dramatist (better than) poet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "and."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"And"** is a conjunction that connects two words or phrases of the same type, indicating that both are included in the statement.
 
• In this sentence, **"Shakespeare was both a dramatist and a poet" **means that he was both a writer of plays and a writer of poetry.
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"When not"** suggests a condition or circumstance in which something is not the case.

 
 
• **Example**: *I usually eat breakfast, but when I'm in a hurry, I don't.*
 
 
 
• **"As well as"** is often used to indicate an additional item or action.
 
 
• **Example**: I bought apples as well as oranges at the grocery store.
 
 
 
• **"Or"** is used to present a choice between two options.
 
 
• **Example**: *Do you want tea or coffee?*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

Over the past 20 years, there __has been__ a constant decline in the variety of vegetables that we eat because the native varieties are no longer available.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is No improvement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The present perfect tense is a verb tense that shows an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past or began in the past and continued to the present time.
 
• The structure is given below:
 
 
• Subject + has/have + V3 + object. (active voice)
 
• Object + has/have + been + V3 + subject. (passive voice)
 
 
 
• ​Example:
 
 
• *​He has played some matches for the Indian Cricket team. (active voice)*
 
• *Some matches have been played by him for the Indian Cricket team. (passive voice)*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, we need to follow the structure in the active voice form.
 
• Since the given sentence talks about the action that continues till the present time, 'has been' is the most appropriate choice of the verb form in the** underlined part.**
 
• Thus we are left with the 1st option as the only correct choice.

 

Correct Sentence__: *Over the past 20 years, there **has been** a constant decline in the variety of vegetables that we eat because the native varieties are no longer available.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.**

**(The people of Philippines has voted) **to elect a new president.

options.text: The people of the Philippines have voted
The people of the Philippines has voted
The people of Philippines have voted

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **"******The people of the Philippines have voted."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are two errors in the given sentence.
 
• The first error in the sentence is a subject-verb agreement mistake.
 
• The auxiliary verb **"have"** must be used to match the plural subject** "people."**
 
• The second error is the use of an article.
 
• The reason for using** "the"** is that **"Philippines"** is a proper noun that requires an article when used to refer to a specific country.
 
• The use of **"the"** before **"Philippines" **helps specify that it is a particular group of people in that country who have voted.
 
• Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

Correct sentence: ***The people of the Philippines have voted**__ to elect a new president.*

I am not __use to eat__ spicy and oily food.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When we look at the sentence, we get to know that there is a **mistake in using the phrase 'be used to.'**
 
• **Be used to** means** 'be accustomed to' **or** 'be familiar with'.**
 
• It refers to the past, present, or future.
 
• We normally follow** 'be used to' **with the ***-ing* form of a verb**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

**The correct sentence would be -** *I am not **used to eating__** spicy and oily food.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's understand the concept with some more examples.

 
• I am used to traveling hill stations by bus.
 
• He was not used to having hot soup.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

__Bulbul is honest girl__ but she is also very rude.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

'an' and 'a' are definite articles whereas 'the' is an indefinite article.

'an' is used when the word starts with a vowel sound - that is, 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u' and 'a' is used for words starting with a consonant sound.

Here, 'honest', when pronounced, has a sound of 'o' which is a vowel. So, 'an' must be used before 'honest'.

The correct sentence is: *Bulbul is **an** honest girl but she is also very rude.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Juliet is __telling to__ Ben to complete the work immediately.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**telling**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the usage of the preposition "**to**" is incorrect.
 
• The preposition 'to' is used to indicate a direction, expression of time, link verb, and phrasal verb.
 
• The preposition 'to' is used before verbs as **infinitive**.
 
 
• **Example**: To play, to fight, to write.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the verb "**telling**" is a **gerund**.
 
• The **prepositions **are usually used before the **gerund**.
 
• The usage of "**to**" is not adding to the meaning of the sentence and looks like irregular usage.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 4**.

 

The correct sentence is__: *Juliet is __telling__ Ben to complete the work immediately.*

Don’t use those pencils; __use the one __we bought in Portugal.
questions.solution:

__
 
• Here, **'ones' **refer to **'pencils'** which is plural, therefore we will use it as it is also plural.
 
• A pronoun must agree with its antecedent (the noun to which it refers) in both number and gender.
 
• We use 'one' and 'ones' -
 
 
• after an adjective__:
 __
 
• Example: *Which is your car, the red **one **or the black one? *(here, one refers to 'car')
 
 
 
• after 'the'__:
 
 
• Example: *Let us look at the photographs - the **ones** you took in Delhi. *(here, ones refers to 'photographs')
 
 
 
• after which in questions:
 
 
• Example: *You can have one toy. Which **one** do you want?* (here, one refers to 'toy')
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate substitute is **'use the ones'**.

• The phrase **"had seen" **correctly implies that the witnessing of the accident occurred **before the action of telephoning** the police.
 
• When **two incidents happen** in **the past one by one**, we use **past perfect tense for the first incident** and **simple past for the second incident.**
 
• **Here accident had occurred first then the man telephoned.**
 
• The structure **"had seen the accident occur"** correctly uses the **past perfect tense** to indicate the sequence of events.

Therefore, the correct answer is-* "The man who **had seen the accident occur__** telephoned the police."*

• **Option 1 ("saw the accident was occurring")** implies that the accident was in the process of happening, but is awkward and does not clearly convey that the action of seeing was completed before he telephoned.
 
• **Option 2 ("saw the accident occurred") **is grammatically incorrect because "saw" and "occurred" do not correctly align in a sequence of events.
